fixes.explanation: Yes, baker! The Lord says, "I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty." A Father. I know a thing or two about being called Papa, and it's the best name I've got.

Not quite, friend. Paul asks what partnership righteousness can have with wickedness, and what fellowship light has with darkness. He's asking because the answer is none. These pairs don't team up, and that's his whole point.

True, baker! God says, "I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people." Dwell with them AND walk among them. That's a God who promises to live right there with His people.

Ooh, I'd flip that one back, friend! It's true. The words Paul quotes say, "I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people." God promises to dwell with them and walk among them, and that promise is a big one.

Nice try, friend, but a temple trip isn't in this line. The Lord says, "Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord." Paul did just say "we are the temple of the living God," so I see how the temple stuck in your head. But the call here is to come out and be separate.
False is right, baker! The Lord says, "Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you." Turned away? Nowhere in that line! The Lord's answer to His people is that He will receive them.

Knowing things is great, friend, but that's not the word Paul uses here. He writes, "…let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God." The word that fits the blank is holiness. Knowledge can wait in the pantry for this one.
